title: High thermoelectric performance at room temperature of n-type Mg3Bi2-based materials by Se doping

nodes.label: Near-room-temperature thermoelectrics are dominated by scarce, costly Bi2Te3, so a Te-free n-type material is wanted
n-type Mg3Sb2-based Zintl materials perform poorly near room temperature
Alloying towards Mg3Bi2 and doping with Se should lift the carrier concentration while keeping mobility high
Mg3.2Bi1.4Sb0.6 Zintl solid solution with excess Mg to secure n-type conduction

attrs.reason: 70% Mg3Bi2 narrows the gap; excess Mg fills the vacancies that would make it p-type

nodes.label: Substitute Se for Sb as the electron donor
Se content x = 0, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02 and 0.04 per formula unit
Ball milling then DC hot pressing, a short hot cycle chosen to leave coarse grains

attrs.reason: few grain boundaries means little boundary scattering of carriers

nodes.label: Ball mill the elemental charge for 10 h
DC hot press the powder at 1053 K and 45 MPa for 2 min
Every composition is single-phase Mg3Sb2-type (P-3m1) with no impurity reflections
The body is dense and cleaves along layers, exposing coarse facets tens of microns across
Mg, Bi, Sb and Se are distributed through the body without segregation
Se substitution brings the K-point conduction valley down to the Fermi level, raising the valley degeneracy
Carrier concentration rises from 0.55 to 3.4e19 cm-3 with Se while mobility stays at 127-168 cm2/V/s
Se donates electrons on the anion site, the extra valley absorbs them without raising the effective mass, and coarse grains leave the mobility intact
Room-temperature resistivity collapses from ~600 to ~11 uohm m, and the Seebeck magnitude falls from 350 to 175-239 uV/K
Power factor reaches 29 uW/cm/K2 at room temperature for x = 0.01
Lattice thermal conductivity falls to 0.60-0.70 W/m/K, half the undoped value
The power-factor gain and the suppressed lattice conduction together outweigh the Seebeck loss and the added electronic heat flow
ZT is 0.82 at 300 K and peaks at 1.24 near 498 K
As a module leg from 300 to 623 K it gives an engineering ZT near 0.84 and about 12% conversion efficiency

attrs.condition: cold side 300 K, hot side up to 623 K

nodes.label: The room-temperature ZT beats every reported Te- or Se-doped Mg3Sb2-based material and matches n-type Bi2Te3
Se doping of a Bi-rich Mg3Sb2 Zintl gives a Te-free n-type thermoelectric that works at room temperature
Reported Te-, Sc-, Y- and Se-doped Mg3Sb2 datasets and n-type Bi2Te3 as the room-temperature incumbent
Single parabolic band Pisarenko relation, Wiedemann-Franz for the electronic heat flow, and the engineering ZT formalism
Mobility drops away above 450 K, attributed to vacancies left by Mg loss at high temperature
At x = 0.01 the Se content is near the EDS detection limit, so its map cannot establish uniform Se distribution
All five patterns fall on the Mg3Sb2 stick pattern with no extra reflections at any Se level

F5b: -350, -260, -212, -208, -178 uV/K. Two conflicts with the text: it says 'the resistivity increases first, and reaches the maximum limit when x = 0.01' where the panel shows a minimum there (the sentence appears to mean conductivity), and it says 'both the resistivity and Seebeck coefficient continuously increase with the increasing temperature' where the undoped resistivity falls with temperature throughout and the undoped Seebeck magnitude peaks near 400 K and then falls.

panel_conditions.condition: cold side held at 300 K, hot side varied up to 623 K

notes: Lost: the mobility-vs-carrier-concentration comparison panel F4c, the total thermal conductivity panel F5d, the crystal-structure drawing F1a, the plain band structures F2a/F2b (read but folded into o2's image_note) and the engineering power factor F7a. Audits: the Se EDS map is at or below the detection limit so it cannot show uniform Se (o4, n27); the text says resistivity rises to a maximum at x = 0.01 where F5a shows it falling monotonically with Se, and says both resistivity and Seebeck rise with temperature where the undoped resistivity falls (o8); mobility drops away above 450 K (o6, n26); and the engineering values read 0.84 and 11.8% against the 0.9 and 12% quoted in the text (o13). Packet defect: the F4b ordinate carries the carrier-concentration units of F4a rather than mobility units, and the OCR misreads two panel letters (F2b as q, F5b as g), both flagged as detector/OCR disagreements.

changes: Removed n16 -counteracts-> n17. The graph carried both causes and counteracts between the same pair, which asserts and denies the same link. n16 bundles the resistivity collapse and the Seebeck loss, and its net effect on the power factor is the causes edge; the Seebeck loss term is already named in n19 (MEC/tradeoff), which is where v04 puts it.

n16 and n17 property_family thermal -> electrical. Resistivity, Seebeck coefficient and the power factor S^2/rho are electrical transport quantities; n18 (lattice thermal conductivity) keeps thermal, so the trade-off in n19 is now between the two families it actually runs across.

o8 label and image_note rewritten against the F5a and F5b crops. The old note said resistivity falls monotonically with Se and that this contradicts the text; the panel actually shows a minimum at x = 0.01 (600 / 23 / 11.5 / 13 / 15 uohm m), so the previous audit was stated unfairly. The conflict with the text is real but is one of sign - the text's 'resistivity ... reaches the maximum limit at x = 0.01' describes a minimum in the panel - and the separate temperature-dependence conflict, which was correct, is now stated with both the resistivity and the Seebeck evidence.

panel_checks.note: F3f is the Se map, labelled 'Se' and '(f)', at a 50 um scale bar, and it is sparse single-pixel noise with no resolvable structure. The audit (n27: at x = 0.01 the Se content is near the EDS detection limit, so the map cannot establish uniform Se) is exactly what the panel shows, and image_support=partial is right.

F4b is the Hall mobility against temperature for the five compositions, with T^-0.5, T^-1 and T^-1.5 guides. The node's packet-defect claim is verified on the crop: the ordinate reads 'mu_H (10^19 cm^-3)', i.e. it carries F4a's carrier-concentration units instead of cm2 V-1 s-1. Values at 300 K are ~170 (x=0.01), 160 (0.005), 148 (0.02), 127 (0.04) and ~15 (x=0), matching the node.

F5a is resistivity and F5b the Seebeck coefficient, both against temperature for the five compositions - the right panels. The node's reading of them was not right: F5a shows a minimum at x = 0.01, not a monotonic fall with Se, so the audit had to be restated. Corrected in place.

review.audit_summary: Four audits (o4/n27, o6/n26, o8, o13), at the edge of budget but each one changing support. Three were stated fairly. The fourth, o8, was not: it announced a figure-against-text contradiction on a reading of F5a that the panel does not support, which is the failure mode the round-4 checklist asks the judge to catch. It has been rewritten - there is still a real conflict, but it is a sign error in the text's sentence rather than a monotonicity claim, and the temperature-dependence half of the audit (the undoped resistivity falls where the text says all of them rise) is the sounder part. The remaining three are correctly graded as 'the figure does not resolve it' (o4's Se map below the detection limit) or 'the panel value is slightly below the quoted one' (o13: 0.84 and 11.8% against 0.9 and 12%), not as contradictions.
